text: With the warehouse reliably filling every night, this lesson builds the first thing a Riverside employee actually sees: a single-store, parameterized SSRS report each of the fourteen store managers opens every morning.

The dataset is one query against fact_sales, filtered by a StoreId parameter and the prior business day, grouped by category and sorted by net sales descending -- so a manager sees what moved and what didn't without sorting anything themselves.

Data isolation comes from the parameter itself: it's hidden in the published report, and each manager's subscription passes a fixed, hardcoded store ID -- so a manager's version of this report is physically incapable of returning another store's rows.
Deployment is fourteen data-driven subscriptions, one per store, each emailing that manager at 7:30 -- after the load's 7 a.m. checkpoint, with ninety minutes of margin before the doors open at nine.
The first deliverable in the brief is live and in managers' inboxes. Next: the foundation for the VP's side of the platform -- the Power BI semantic model.
